subject.title: [Bug]: Slack reaction_added/reaction_removed events never delivered via Socket Mode (multi-account, v2026.3.24)

question: Should maintainers require live current-main Slack Socket Mode reaction evidence before any fix PR for this report?
rationale: Current source has handlers and plausible drop boundaries, but the report lacks raw envelopes or current-main logs that identify whether Slack/Bolt delivery, account filtering, or authorization is the first failing layer.

options.title: Require live reaction proof
options.body: Keep the issue open and block code work until redacted current-main Socket Mode envelopes, gateway trace logs, and channel status output show the first drop boundary.

options.title: Sponsor live diagnosis
options.body: Have a maintainer run a real multi-account Slack Socket Mode repro and then decide whether a narrow Slack plugin fix is safe.

options.title: Fold into broader Socket Mode report
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/89222 as canonical only if maintainers confirm the broad report covers reaction envelopes with comparable evidence.

recommendation.title: Require live reaction proof
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and block code work until redacted current-main Socket Mode envelopes, gateway trace logs, and channel status output show the first drop boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The routing fix linked from the older reaction reports makes Vincent the best available owner for deciding whether new live proof is required before another Slack reaction fix.
